deviceCheck.badFile: This file is not a run file of this check.
deviceCheck.cloudNote: If this device cannot answer a case, the request goes to Firebase AI Logic in the cloud with the same invented input. It is counted as a cloud run, never as an on-device one, and listed under “Leaving your device”. Cases that may only run on this device are never sent.
deviceCheck.deductionsNotRead: The deductions were left out and marked “not read on this device”.
deviceCheck.headline.incomeRight: readings with every yearly-income input right
deviceCheck.headline.notFound: · {count} with a value not found (left empty, to be typed in)
deviceCheck.headline.wrong: readings in which a wrong value reached the person (this must be 0)
deviceCheck.headline.wrongNone: readings in which a wrong value reached the person: none, as required
deviceCheck.lead: Runs a fixed set of invented test cases through Firebase AI Logic and the app’s own tasks, and records where each one actually ran. No personal data is used.
deviceCheck.noModel.android: This phone has no on-device model available (Gemini Nano through AICore is not supported here or not ready), so the check cannot run here. A recording made on a device that has one can be shown below.
deviceCheck.noModel.ios: This iPhone has no on-device model available (Apple Intelligence is off, not supported, or its model is not ready), so the check cannot run here. A recording made on a device that has one can be shown below.
deviceCheck.noModel.web: This browser has no on-device model, so the check cannot run here. A recording made in a browser that has one can be shown below.
deviceCheck.ran.afterDevice: In the cloud, after a failed on‑device attempt
deviceCheck.recordingNote: This is a recording, not a live run. It was made on the machine named above and is shown exactly as it was saved.
deviceCheck.repeat: Run each extraction case 3 times, to see how stable the device’s reading is
deviceCheck.scoredByValue: Scored by value: a field is right when the placeholder answered holds the expected value, whichever placeholder that is. “Expected value in” lists every placeholder that holds it.
deviceCheck.summary: Where each case was finally answered: {onDevice} of {total} on this device; {afterDevice} in the cloud after a failed on-device attempt; {inCloud} in the cloud; {notRun} did not run.
deviceCheck.summaryFinal: What the person ends up with, after the checks and any retry: {correct} of {fields} fields correct; {retried} extraction cases were repeated in the cloud.
deviceCheck.summaryFirst: First attempt: {firstOnDevice} of {total} were tried on this device. Extraction, first answer: {correct} of {fields} fields correct.
deviceCheck.summaryIncome: Yearly-income inputs all right (gross pay, year to date, pay frequency, period and pay dates), in what the person ends up with: {correct} of {total} extraction cases.
deviceCheck.summaryIncomeSplit: Yearly-income inputs (gross pay, year to date, pay frequency, period and pay dates), in what the person ends up with, over {total} readings: all right in {right}; some not found (left empty, none wrong) in {notFound}; some wrong in {wrong}.
deviceCheck.summaryNotRead: Answered on this device with the deductions not read: {count}.
deviceCheck.summaryRepetitions: Each extraction case was run {repetitions} times; every run is counted as one reading.
deviceCheck.summaryWrong: Readings in which any value reached the person wrong: {wrong} of {total}.
deviceCheck.title: On‑device check
deviceCheck.wrongMustBeZero: A value not found is shown as empty and can be typed in. A wrong value may go unnoticed, so the number of wrong values that reach the person must be zero.
error.appCheckTryAgain: The app could not get the check that shows the cloud service this request comes from the real app, so the silhouette was not sent. This happens now and then and is nothing you did. Try again; if it keeps happening, type the numbers instead.
judges.checking.android: Checking whether this phone has the on-device model…
judges.checking.ios: Checking whether this iPhone has the on-device model…
judges.checking.web: Checking whether this browser has the on-device model…
judges.lead: Three steps, one button each. Everything here is invented: a prepared household and a sample paystub.
judges.step1.body: Fills in the answers of an invented household and shows the results that the rules on this device give it. Nothing is sent.
judges.step1.button: Fill in and see the results
judges.step1.title: Run the Quick Check for a prepared household
judges.step2.body: Shows the sample paystub with every value replaced by a placeholder. Send it, and Firebase AI Logic points at the fields by placeholder; only the silhouette can leave.
judges.step2.title: Open the sample paystub and see its silhouette
judges.step3.body.android: Opens “Leaving your device”: each request that left, as the app built it, and each answer that stayed on this device.
judges.step3.body.ios: Opens “Leaving your device”: each request that left, as the app built it, and each answer that stayed on this device.
judges.step3.body.web: Opens “Leaving your device”: each request that left, byte for byte, and each answer that stayed on this device.
judges.step3.title: Compare what left
judges.title: Try it in two minutes
judges.withModel.android: This phone has the on-device model: in step 2 the silhouette is read on this device first, and nothing leaves when that reading passes its checks. If the device cannot read it reliably, the silhouette (never the values) is sent to the cloud. A program page can explain your own result here.
judges.withModel.ios: This iPhone has the on-device model: in step 2 the silhouette is read on this device first, and nothing leaves when that reading passes its checks. If the device cannot read it reliably, the silhouette (never the values) is sent to the cloud. A program page can explain your own result here.
judges.withModel.web: This browser has the on-device model: in step 2 the silhouette is read on this device first, and nothing leaves when that reading passes its checks. If the device cannot read it reliably, the silhouette (never the values) is sent to the cloud. A program page can explain your own result here.
judges.withoutModel.android: This phone has no on-device model available: step 2 sends the silhouette (never the values) to Firebase AI Logic in the cloud. Offline, the sample’s answer key is used instead. With Gemini Nano ready on this phone, step 2 runs on this device.
judges.withoutModel.ios: This iPhone has no on-device model available: step 2 sends the silhouette (never the values) to Firebase AI Logic in the cloud. Offline, the sample’s answer key is used instead. With Apple Intelligence on, step 2 runs on this device.
judges.withoutModel.web: This browser has no on-device model: step 2 sends the silhouette (never the values) to Firebase AI Logic in the cloud. Offline, the sample’s answer key is used instead. With Chrome’s on-device model, step 2 runs on this device.
